findings.title: Punch/Clap courtesy ceiling calls a 1–2 kg-TNT release harmless while the same bay draws eardrums bursting at 5 m; 'Rattle the windows' preset = damage risk to 1 km
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js:3040 (shock), 3093, 3100; src/app.html effortReadout (~2945) and bayClap/bayPunch blast blocks (~1470-1500)
findings.evidence: Unlimited strength, Clap, preset 'Courtesy ceiling': verdict 'His hands meet at 340 m/s and release 1.8 kg TNT.' / 'Effort: as hard as lifting 7,260 t. The most he can use before something nearby comes to harm.' Same bay's chart (aria-label): 'Windows shatter 16.4 m; Houses collapse 6.41 m; Eardrums start to burst 5.59 m; Lung damage 3.65 m'. Bay text: 'That makes a comic “thunderclap” fair physics: two hands’ worth of energy, released in a small space.' Punch at its ceiling: chart 'Eardrums start to burst 4.47 m'. Punch, preset 'Rattle the windows': 'The least effort that rattles windows and ornaments 5 m away' but the hazard list says 'Air blast loud enough to risk damage within 5 m ...; now out to 820 m from him' (clap: 1.03 km). Cause: shock(v,E) = v >= 340 m/s ? E : 0, so 339 m/s counts zero blast and 340 m/s counts the full energy. The Mach-1 rule is stated only in README, not on the page.
findings.expected: One rule on one page. Either the bay's blast chart (an upper bound, labelled so) is also what the hazard uses, or a subsonic release is shown as a thump with no damage chart. The 'Rattle' preset should not be the same effort as a damaging blast reaching 820 m.
findings.fix: For subsonic punches/claps, replace blastBlock with 'subsonic: a thump, not a blast wave (the lab counts a blast only past Mach 1)' and drop the 'thunderclap' sentence; state the Mach-1 rule in the courtesy-ceiling card; in the rattle preset readout, say when its first onset coincides with the sonic boom and a damaging blast.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD 0ab5706 (snapshot build; scripts in scratchpad/review1/js/f1.js and f1n.js). Engine: clap at 7.29e6 kg-force gives vHand 340.26 m/s, air reach 0; at 7.30e6 kg-force, 340.49 m/s, air reach 1,026 m. The energy is about the same (7.66 MJ), so 0.2% more effort turns a blast counted as zero into risk of damage out to 1 km. Page, unlimited strength, Clap, 'Courtesy ceiling': 'His hands meet at 340 m/s and release 1.8 kg TNT.' / 'The most he can use before something nearby comes to harm.' The same bay's chart shows 'Eardrums start to burst 5.59 m' (beyond the 5 m 'near') and still says 'That makes a comic “thunderclap” fair physics'. 'Rattle the windows' sits at the next probe, where 'Air blast ... now out to 1.03 km from him' (punch: 820 m). The page never states the Mach-1 rule; it is only in README:82. The Collide tab and the duo Collide use a different rule (release time × a0 against the damage radius), so the page has two blast rules. Physics note: for a clap the closing speed is 2·vHand, and air squeezed out between the palms leaves faster than that, so gating on vHand < a0 is the weakest part of the rule.
verdict.better_fix: Make the page state and follow one rule. (a) In bayPunch/bayClap, when the speed is below K.a0 and silent strike is off, replace blastBlock with callout('Below Mach 1 the lab counts this as a thump, not a blast wave. If all of it went into the air it would be ' + fmtTNT(r.E) + ' (an upper bound the courtesy ceiling does not use).'). Show the 'thunderclap' sentence only when r.vHand >= K.a0. (b) EFF_HAZ.air.what: '... (counted only once something he moves passes Mach 1)'. (c) In effortReadout for a preset, when hazard boom/air starts at the same effort (res.use <= use), add 'At this effort it also breaks the sound barrier, and the blast risks damage out to ' + fmtDist(rc.air) + '.'

outcome.change: Punch and Clap show a subsonic release as a thump (no blast chart), as the ceiling and Collide treat it; 'thunderclap' only past Mach 1; the ceiling card states the rule.

verdict.better_fix: engine.js jump(): landRatio = landed && !ctx.groundHolds ? landF / RB : 0; Eground: landRatio > 1 && !soft ? Eland : 0. findings.title: Walk tab canon sentence says 'It takes a stomp' / 'nothing short of a stomp', which the Stomp tab refutes at the same settings
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html:3150-3151
findings.evidence: Walk, default (concrete, 100 short tons): 'Presence stops being harmless when plaster 3 m away may crack: not even when he stamps. It takes a stomp (see the Stomp tab).' Stomp tab, near 3 m, preset 'Crack the plaster next door': 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t shake the ground enough that plaster may crack 3 m away.' Walk on granite: 'a glass 3 m away ripples with nothing short of a stomp, and people 3 m away feel nothing short of a stomp.' Stomp on granite, near 3 m: 'Even all-out he can’t make a stomp people feel 3 m away.' Engine: all-out stomp at the default dial gives 2.89 mm/s at 3 m on concrete (plaster 7.6/12.7) and 0.015 mm/s vertical on granite (glass 0.2, feel 0.3); granite needs about 10^7-10^9 kg-force.

findings.fix: Evaluate P.stomp(ctx) with RESTRAINT.MOVES.stomp.shake at 3 m; if it falls short, say 'not even an all-out stomp at this strength'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD (f3.js, f3p.js, f3q.js). Walk, default (concrete, 100 short tons): 'Presence stops being harmless when plaster 3 m away may crack: not even when he stamps. It takes a stomp (see the Stomp tab).' Engine: an all-out stomp at the default dial gives 2.89 mm/s at 3 m on concrete, under both the walking plaster level (7.6) and the single-event level (12.7). It takes about 1e6–1e7 kg-force. Stomp tab, near 3 m, 'Crack the plaster next door': 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t shake the ground enough that plaster may crack 3 m away.' Granite: Walk says 'a glass 3 m away ripples with nothing short of a stomp, and people 3 m away feel nothing short of a stomp'. An all-out stomp gives 0.015 mm/s vertical and 0.005 mm/s side-to-side (glass 0.2, feel 0.3), and the Stomp tab says 'Even all-out he can’t make a stomp most people can just feel 3 m away'. verdict.better_fix: In bayWalk, compute the all-out stomp for the walker: const so = P.stomp(walkers[0][0] === 'Ollie' ? ctxOllie() : c), src = P.RESTRAINT.MOVES.stomp.shake(so, { surface: sf, body: wB }), vS = P.ppvAt(src, 3), vSH = P.ppvAt(src, 3, true). For each threshold that walking can't reach, write vS (or vSH for the glass) >= TH[k] ? 'an all-out stomp (see the Stomp tab)' : 'not even an all-out stomp at this strength'. Replace 'It takes a stomp' and 'nothing short of a stomp' with that text.

outcome.change: The canon sentence evaluates an all-out stomp at the current strength (the Stomp tab's model) instead of assuming one.

findings.title: On sand/soft clay, Sprint, Throw and Jump count footprints as 'the ground gives way' (harm); least-disruptive Sprint is 'Top speed: 0 m/s'
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js:3107 (sprint ground), 3048 (throw), 3065 (jump) vs 3041 SOIL rule used only for stomp
findings.evidence: Sprint, loose sand, default: 'Top speed: 0 m/s.' / 'The most he can do with nothing nearby harmed. verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD 0ab5706 (f5p.js). Sprint on loose sand, default: 'Effort: 3.3% ... verdict.better_fix: engine.js RESTRAINT.MOVES: throw.ground: (r, o) => !SOIL.has(o.surface && o.surface.id) && r.canMove && r.sinkRatio > 1; jump.ground: (r, o) => !SOIL.has(o.surface && o.surface.id) && r.groundFails (or, in soil, only a crater/Eground-based failure); sprint.ground: (r, o) => !SOIL.has(o.surface && o.surface.id) && !!r.sinks && r.vTop > 0. outcome.change: Soil rule for every move: sinking into sand, gravel or clay is a footprint, not broken ground; Sprint, Throw and Jump defaults now reach their goals on sand.

findings.evidence: Rendered rows, both 'Verified': 'Growth: airblast levels that rattle houses... Rattling complaints begin above about 120 dB on a 6 Hz meter, roughly 36 Pa unfiltered' and 'Comic switches: airblast at which people start to notice rattling: about 120 dB (20 Pa)'. RI 8485 (fetched, pp. 58/66) says only 'complaints about rattling occur at airblast levels exceeding about 120 dB (6Hz)'. 36 Pa is the researcher's conversion (129 dB at 6 Hz ≡ 134 dB at 0.1 Hz, so 120 → 125 dB → 35.6 Pa), as the fact's own notes say ('our conversion'). The ceiling card presents '36 Pa air blast, where rattling complaints start' as sourced.
findings.expected: A number not seen in the source should be labelled derived, with its formula. The two rows should not give two different pressures for the same onset.
findings.fix: Move the 36 Pa conversion into its own derived fact (formula and the 6 Hz/0.1 Hz equivalence assumption) and cite that from DP_RATTLE. Relabel the comic row as '120 dB as read on a 6 Hz meter (20 Pa on that meter; about 36 Pa unfiltered, derived)'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced at HEAD. Rendered Sources rows, both VERIFIED: 'Growth: airblast levels that rattle houses ... Rattling complaints begin above about 120 dB on a 6 Hz meter, roughly 36 Pa unfiltered' and 'Comic switches: airblast at which people start to notice rattling: about 120 dB (20 Pa)'. The notes of growth_airblast_usbm_ri8485 call 36 Pa 'our conversion': 129 dB on the 6 Hz meter ≡ 134 dB on the 0.1 Hz meter, so 120 → 125 dB → 35.6 Pa. That is a derived number shown under a Verified badge. R.DP_RATTLE = 36 cites it, and the ceiling card presents '36 Pa air blast, where rattling complaints start' as if sourced. The 5 dB shift is an assumption that fits long mine-blast spectra. For the short, sharp blasts of a punch or clap, a 6 Hz high-pass barely changes the peak, so 20 Pa may be the better onset there. That is one more reason to label the conversion and its assumption. The two rows can be reconciled by meter basis, but the comic row's label gives 20 Pa without the meter.
verdict.better_fix: Split out a derived fact 'airblast_rattle_onset_unfiltered' (status derived: 120 dB on a 6 Hz meter + 5 dB, from the safe-level pairs 129 dB (6 Hz) ≡ 134 dB (0.1 Hz) = 35.6 Pa; assumes a mine-blast spectrum; for short sharp pulses the 6 Hz reading is close to unfiltered, about 20 Pa). Remove '36 Pa' from the verified growth_airblast_usbm_ri8485 display. Point DP_RATTLE's comment at the new fact. Relabel the comic row 'about 120 dB on a 6 Hz meter (20 Pa as read on that meter)'. In the ceiling card, write 'a 36 Pa air blast (our conversion of where rattling complaints start)'.

outcome.change: 36 Pa split into its own derived fact (airblast_rattle_onset_unfiltered, with the formula); the comic row relabelled as 120 dB on a 6 Hz meter.

findings.title: The 'Compared with an elephant' tile sets Rex on any surface against an elephant measured on sandy ground
findings.location: src/app.html bayWalk (ratioE, elSub); src/engine.js VIB.ELEPHANT
findings.evidence: The anchor is Steinmann et al. 2025 Fig. 3f, 'elephant, NWP05, 20 m'; NWP05 'is located on sandy dry ground' (confirmed in the fetched PDF). Default page (concrete): '6× the elephant — one measured walking past 20 m away; inside the 0.15–8× real elephants vary'. The same model on loose sand (review1/shimmer.js): soft-footed 20× and ordinary 66× the anchor, outside the band. On granite: 0.02× ('50× quieter'). The page never says the elephant was on sand.
findings.expected: The site sets the anchor (the lab's own elephant_steinmann2025_site_spread shows ×70–110 between stations), so a like-for-like comparison uses the same ground. Otherwise the page should say the grounds differ and not claim Rex is 'inside' the elephant band.
findings.fix: Compute the elephant ratio with Rex on the 'sand' ground constants (the anchor's ground), whatever surface is selected, and say 'on sandy ground like the elephant's'. Or show the elephant's ground and drop the 'inside the 0.15–8×' sub-line when the surface isn't sand.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced at HEAD. VIB.ELEPHANT's own comment says the anchor elephant was 'on sandy ground' (Steinmann 2025, NWP05 'sandy dry ground', per the verified research notes). The page never says this ('sandy' appears nowhere in app.html, static-data.js or README). bayWalk computes ratioE with the selected surface. Rex soft-footed (vd script) on concrete 5.6×, asphalt 5.6×, gravel 3.8×, loose sand 20×, soft clay 15×, granite 0.016×. Rendered: concrete '6× the elephant, one measured walking past 20 m away; inside the 0.15–8× real elephants vary'; sand '20× the elephant' (outside the band); granite '60× quieter'. outcome.change: The elephant comparison always puts Rex and Ollie on the elephant's sandy ground and says so.

findings.location: src/app.html duoPlanFor (line 3153: floor `need = WALK_LOAD·m·g/1.4`, enough to walk but not to run) and resolveDuoEffort (3173-3184)
findings.evidence: review1/s10-weak.js and s18-fresh.js, fresh visit, Rex + Ollie → Collide. Box: 'Effort: 3.3% of his strength (each pushes as hard as lifting 3 t). The hardest both can go while nothing around them breaks. Courtesy ceiling: 3.3%… Past that, the hit’s air blast risks damage 5 m away.' Verdict: 'Ollie can’t charge. When the harm search finds harm at or just above that floor, use the floor and show the 'Nothing is harmless here' note, or treat 'can’t charge' as an unmet goal and say so. A separate question for the physics lens: does a 2.6 m/s bump really count as a damaging air blast (all of the collision energy treated as an explosion, with 100 Pa at 5 m)?

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (vux/u3.js, u3b.js, u3c.js, u3d.js). On a fresh visit, Collide reads 'Effort: 3.3%… (each pushes as hard as lifting 3 t). The hardest both can go while nothing around them breaks. Courtesy ceiling: 3.3%… Past that, the hit’s air blast risks damage 5 m away.' The verdict is 'Ollie can’t charge… can’t hold up his own weight… Try Set speed.' At a custom 3.17 t, Ollie hits at 2.64 m/s, freeing 8.03 kJ over a 240 ms plush squash, and the page calls that 'the hit’s air blast risks damage 5 m away'. The root cause is wrong physics. duoHarm's win(Q) treats any collision energy as an explosive charge: P.blastRadius(8 kJ, 100 Pa) is about 100 m. But the engine's own rule (RESTRAINT, engine.js ~3031) says energy is an air blast only when released faster than sound: `shock = (v, E) => (v >= K.a0 ? E : 0)`. A 2.6 m/s bump over 240 ms is a thump. Wrestle → Throw has the same defect. On opening it shows 'Rex can’t throw Ollie', and its ceiling is set by 'the landing’s air blast' from Ollie landing at 7.4 m/s after a 2.8 m fall (custom 3.32 t). So two of the four duo tabs open on a non-result capped by a hazard that doesn't exist. Major: wrong physics on the default view.
verdict.better_fix: Apply the solo supersonic rule in duoHarm (src/app.html ~3102-3146). Wrestle throw: replace `win(t.r.Eimpact)` with `win(P.RESTRAINT.MOVES.throw.blast(t.r))`, which already returns 0 unless the landing is supersonic or relativistic. Collide: `const Qblast = r.relativistic || r.outcome === 'boltsLate' ? Q : 0;` and test `win(Qblast)` (or the Collide tab's own thump rule). Then floor charge plans at what running needs: in duoPlanFor, for act === 'collide' && state.colMode === 'charge' && state.colSrc !== 'set', use `lo = Math.max(lo, 1.05 * Math.max(state.m, state.oM) * g)`. Note: fix commit 3454988 adds a thump rule for Collide (which now opens on an 18.1 m/s charge), but line 3169 still uses `win(t.r.Eimpact)` for Wrestle → Throw. That tab still opens on 'Rex can’t throw Ollie', capped by the landing's 'air blast'.

outcome.change: duoHarm('collide') uses the Collide tab's own thump rule (no blast when the hit lasts longer than sound takes to cross the damage zone); the default charge now runs, with 'no cap needed'.

findings.title: Walk tab's 'Show the math' hard-codes Rex's scaled heel-strike numbers and contradicts itself for other bodies
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html:3139
findings.evidence: pw-walk-math.js with {action:'walk', build:'human', H:2, m:180}. The page prints: "The landing adds a pulse of 0.13× his weight lasting 30 ms: an ordinary heel strike stops 11% of him at 0.70 m/s in 37 ms (Baines 2018, scaled)". The engine scales the heel strike as 0.57 m/s × √(h/0.9) and 30 ms × √(h/0.9), with h = 0.45·H. For H = 2 m that is 0.57 m/s in 30 ms; only Rex's 3.048 m gives 0.70 m/s in 37 ms. The same sentence then contradicts its own 'lasting 30 ms'.
findings.expected: The quoted speed and time should be computed for the walker shown.
findings.fix: Build the text from WALK.HS: speedOnly(HS.v·sc) and fmtTime(HS.t·sc) with sc = √(st.h/HS.h). A pulse with a 0.43 shape could also be expressed via st.Tpulse at e = 0.5.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with review1/vc/walkmath.js. With {action:'walk', build:'human', H:2, m:180} (hip 0.9 m) the page says '0.13× his weight lasting 30 ms: an ordinary heel strike stops 11% of him at 0.70 m/s in 37 ms'. With {action:'walk', H:6, m:24056} (hip 2.7 m) it says 'lasting 52 ms … at 0.70 m/s in 37 ms'. The engine (walkStep) uses v = 0.57·√(h/0.9) and t = 0.03·√(h/0.9). That gives 0.57 m/s in 30 ms at h = 0.9 m and 0.99 m/s in 52 ms at h = 2.7 m. Only the 3.048 m Rex (h = 1.3716 m, factor 1.2345) gives 0.70 m/s in 37 ms. The string is hard-coded at app.html:3139.
verdict.better_fix: At app.html:3139, build the numbers from the engine: `const sc = Math.sqrt(st.h / P.WALK.HS.h);` and replace 'at 0.70 m/s in 37 ms' with `'at ' + speedOnly(P.WALK.HS.v * sc) + ' in ' + fmtTime(P.WALK.HS.t * sc)`. The working tree's walkStep now returns heelV and heelT for this: use st.heelV and st.heelT.

outcome.change: Walk math computes the heel speed and time from the walker's hip height.
